**In the following question, some part of the sentence may have errors. Find out which part of the sentence has an error and select the appropriate option. If a sentence is free from error, select 'No Error'.**

Companies in countries as the United States (1)/ left out of the trade pacts could face (2)/ disadvantages when trying to tap fast growing Asian markets. (3)/ No error (4)
questions.solution:
**Correct option - 1**

Here, concept of preposition is brought under consideration. We often get confused between like & S. **Like **is used as preposition before noun to should relativeness. Whereas, **as **is used to describe function of a person or thing. Here, **the United States **is a proper noun and it is not performing any action. So, preposition **like **should be used instead of **as. **Hence, option 1 is the correct answer.

**Correct sentence - **Companies in countries like the United States left out of the trade pacts could face disadvantages when trying to tap fast growing Asian markets.

questions.solution:

Here, concept of subject - verb agreement is brought under consideration. Since, subject **increasing dependence **is a 3rd person singular noun. Hence, the verb used should also be singular. Hence, replace **develop **with **develops. **So, option 1 is the correct answer.

**Correct sentence - **As increasing dependence on information systems develops the need for such systems to be reliable and secure also becomes more essential.

questions.question:
**The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.**

They have / always take / an hour’s walk / before breakfast.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **They have**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• In the sentence, "**take**" is the main verb, and it needs to be in the present tense since the action "**taking an hour's walk**" is a habitual action that happens regularly, not a completed action in the past.
 
• "**They have**" indicates the **present perfect tense**, which is used for actions that started in the past and continue to the present or have just been completed.
 
• "*They always take an hour's walk before breakfast*" is the **correct sentence**.
 
• Here, "**take**" is the present tense verb that agrees with the subject "**they**" and accurately describes the **ongoing habit of taking a walk before breakfast**.
 
• The adverb "**always**" further clarifies the sentence by emphasizing that the action of taking a walk happens habitually, not just in the present.
 
• The present tense is often used for habitual actions, especially when they are part of a daily routine.

Thus, **option 4** is the correct answer.

questions.question:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error. Select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don’t find any error, mark ‘No error’ as your answer. 

Vivek should be excited / on the promotion / he’s got.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'on the promotion'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The erroneous part of the given sentence is **on the promotion.**
 
• There is an error in a **preposition **in this part. 
 
• The **preposition "on" **usually points to something specific, like a location. ** **
 
• Thus, **on **cannot be used in context of the given sentence. 
 
• This makes **option 4 **the correct answer. 
 
• The correct preposition to use here is **about **which usually means the subject of something, or something less specific.

***Correct sentence - ****Vivek should be excited / **about the promotion** / he’s got.*

There was no other book / in the English language / which is as interesting as this one.

options.text: which is as interesting as this one

questions.solution:
The correct answer is Option 1 i.e. **"There was no other book"**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The sentence is talking about a general topic. Hence, it should be in the present tense. It is also mentioned in the last part of the sentence.
 
• The statement is meant to reflect a general, timeless fact or an ongoing situation, changing **"was"** to **"is"** would be appropriate.
 
• **Is** will be used instead of **was.**
 
• The correct usage is "There** is** no other book"

Therefore, the correct complete sentence is *There **is** no other book in the English language which is as interesting as this one.*

questions.question:

Washington Irving’s writing career started at / the tender age of nineteen when he joined / his brother Peter’s newspaper The Morning Chronicle / as journalist.

options.text: his brother Peter’s newspaper The Morning Chronical
Washington Irving’s writing career started at
the tender age of nineteen when he joined

questions.solution:
The correct answer is: "**as journalist.**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• The phrase "**as journalist**" is not a complete sentence and does not have a subject.
 
• A complete sentence would be "**as a journalist**" or "**as the journalist**."
 
• In the context of the sentence, "**as a journalist**" specifies the role or profession that Washington Irving assumed when he joined his brother Peter's newspaper.
 
• It's a grammatical convention to use the indefinite article in such constructions
 
• This is a common error in English, where articles (a, an, the) are omitted before nouns.

Therefore, the correct answer is **option 3**.

**Corrected sentence**: *Washington Irving’s writing career started at the tender age of nineteen when he joined his brother Peter’s newspaper, The Morning Chronicle, as a journalist.*

• The phrase "able to drink" is incorrect in this context. The correct form is "not allowed to drink," as "able" implies physical capability, whereas the sentence intends to convey prohibition. (अनुमति नहीं है)

• The word "allowed" should be used here to indicate that someone is prohibited or restricted from doing something. (स्वीकृत नहीं है)
